subject: biology-2
question: When the body is dehydrated, the pituitary gland releases the hormone **ADH**. What effect does ADH have on the kidneys?

options.text: ADH decreases water reabsorption so that urine volume increases.
ADH increases sodium reabsorption, and water follows into the blood.
ADH raises the glomerular filtration rate so that more urine is produced.
ADH makes the collecting ducts more permeable to water, so more water is reabsorbed and urine becomes concentrated.

explanation: ADH inserts water channel proteins into the cells of the collecting ducts, allowing water to be reabsorbed back into the blood, which concentrates the urine and conserves body water. A and C describe the opposite of this effect. Sodium reabsorption is controlled mainly by aldosterone, so B describes a different hormone's action.
